subject: Atlanta Fed GDPNow (GDP nowcast, US)
headline: Beats the no-change null on 37 quarters of real-time vintages — 75% lower MAE against the advance estimate and 25% lower against the settled number, so the edge is not an artefact of targeting the first print.

findings.question: Is the forecast a model at all, or an accounting identity?
findings.answer: Bridge-equation nowcast; beats the no-change null on MAE by 75% (1.26 vs 5.05 pp)
findings.falsifier: the bridge equations would not aggregate to a GDP path at all, and the MAE ratio would sit at or above 1

findings.question: Does it beat the null out of sample?
findings.answer: 28 of 37 quarters, MAE ratio 0.25 (<1 = beats the null)
findings.falsifier: ratio >= 1.0, i.e. no better than carrying the previous quarter forward

findings.question: Is that skill against the FIRST publication or the settled number?
findings.answer: Against the settled number it still beats the null: MAE ratio 0.31 on all 37 quarters, 0.75 excluding 2020 — the edge narrows but survives
findings.falsifier: a settled-number ratio above 1.0, or one that flips when 2020 is dropped

findings.question: Are the inputs real-time vintages, or revised history?
findings.answer: Real-time vintages (ALFRED) throughout; a vintage that post-dates the forecast is refused by guard_nowcast_predates_release
findings.falsifier: a fixture where the nowcast vintage post-dates the release — the guard would go red and the evaluation would be refused

findings.question: Can the evaluation go red?
findings.answer: Four guards, each mutation-proved: vintage ordering, shared benchmark vintage, first-publication target, units
findings.falsifier: each guard is mutation-proved: the seeded fault makes it read red

limitations: The advantage survives the settled-number target but narrows sharply: 0.25 against the advance estimate, 0.75 against the settled number excluding 2020.
The evaluation uses one public dataset and one target definition; neither has been independently replicated outside this repository.
